readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckLocalization.differential_cutoff
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E=ClosedSmoothModel 3=EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), with its existing Euclidean L2 norm, and let e_i=basis3 i be the standard orthonormal coordinate vectors. Bilin=E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, Jet1=E ->L[R] Bilin, Jet2=E ->L[R] Jet1, and Variables=(Bilin times Jet1) times Jet2. Bilin and both jet spaces carry their existing nested continuous-linear-map operator norms. The four literal letI binders install precisely ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedAddCommGroup and toNormedSpace over RingHom.id R for Jet1 and Jet2. They retain the operator norm and real scalar action; they do not supply free norm dictionaries or replace the norm. Variables has the original nested maximum product norm. The pinned Y and Graph definitions retain the sum of value-sup and scaled-difference-sup norms and the sum of the four u,ut,du,ddu Y norms; their nine-entry Inputs uses the original finite Pi maximum norm. These two latter carriers are not quantified in this declaration, and no norm bound or completion of a derivative graph is asserted here. For every arbitrary background CLM B:E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E, arbitrary DB:E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E, arbitrary G0:Bilin, J0:Jet1, H0:Jet2, c:R, dc:E ->L[R] R, ddc:Bilin, and p:Variables, write h=p.1.1, j=p.1.2 and k=p.2. There are no invertibility, positive-definiteness, symmetry, realized-jet, metric/manifold, smoothness, compact-support, cutoff, time or Holder-exponent hypotheses. Put a_ij=inverseEntries G0 i j, the entries of the existing total Matrix inverse of the matrix G0(e_i)(e_j). For arbitrary h, inverseEntryDerivative G0 i j applied to h is -sum_{r,s} a_ir*a_sj*h(e_r)(e_s), with both inverse factors and all ordered metric slots retained. Put ell=lowerDifferential B DB G0 J0, which is exactly fderiv R of (G,J) |-> DeTurckPrincipalIdentity.lowerTerm B DB G J at (G0,J0), on the original product/CLM dictionaries. The pinned lowerTerm is the full actual Ricci/Lie first-jet remainder, (-2) smul ricciFirstBilin G J + J(fieldValue G J B) + G.comp(fieldFirstOperator G J B DB) + (G.flip.comp(fieldFirstOperator G J B DB)).flip. Thus the differential appearing on both sides is the whole Bilin-valued linear operator D(h,j,k)=sum_{i,j} [-(sum_{r,s} a_ir*a_sj*h(e_r)(e_s))] smul H0(e_i)(e_j) + sum_{i,j} a_ij smul k(e_i)(e_j) + ell(h,j). It includes inverse variation contracted against the base second jet H0 and the actual lower fderiv in both metric and first-jet variables. Its firstOrder coefficient is precisely ell.comp(inr), so firstOrder(v)=ell(0,v); the zeroOrder coefficient includes inverse variation against H0 plus ell(h,0). The cutoff tuple has value c smul h, first jet u |-> c smul j(u)+dc(u) smul h, and second jet (u,v) |-> c smul k(u)(v)+dc(u) smul j(v)+dc(v) smul j(u)+ddc(u)(v) smul h. In particular the precompR term gives the ordered dc(v) smul j(u) contribution and precompL gives the Hessian term ddc(u)(v) smul h; both mixed terms remain separately present. The asserted equality is the full Bilin equality D(cutoffVariables c dc ddc p)=c smul D(p)+sum_{i,j} a_ij smul [dc(e_i) smul j(e_j)+dc(e_j) smul j(e_i)+ddc(e_i)(e_j) smul h]+firstOrder B DB G0 J0(dc.smulRight h). The final firstOrder correction equals ell(0, u |-> dc(u) smul h) and is added with a positive sign. The inverse-variation and zero-order contributions scale by c and stay inside c smul D(p); neither is removed. This is an algebraic localization identity for the pinned total differential CLM at arbitrary formal base jets. It does not itself certify that this CLM is the Frechet derivative of evolution for arbitrary singular G0, construct an actual cutoff germ, establish coordinate covariance, or construct a global L/P/R or physical flow. Those interpretations would need their separate derivative and geometric hypotheses. No term, direction order, original norm or premise was altered in this readback.
